column1: # boru Language Specification: lang-layer Node/Xml surface
# The KERNEL literal grammar (parsing, rendering, entity escaping, ${} holes,
# the syntax negatives) lives in eng/spec/xml-literal.tsv. This file pins the
# LANG-LAYER words over a Node/Xml value: the xml-elem / xml-text / xml-attr
# accessors (native_xml.go), structural equality via deq, and the FlexXml
# Scope note: FlexXml MUTATION (set / append on a flex element) and a
# binding-fed ${} interpolation are RUNTIME builders the bytecode compiler
# faithfully falls back on, so they cannot be spec value rows without
# regressing the never-raise compile-compile failure ceiling — they are covered by
# §1  literals — value, type, membership (exercises XML const-baking in the
#     lang compiled census, the eng-layer twin of eng/spec/xml-literal.tsv)

column3: a self-closing literal renders back to well-formed XML
attributes, a child element and text round-trip
a literal is a Node/Xml value
Node/Xml matches the Xml slot
Node/Xml is a dedicated type, not a Map subtype

column1: # §2  xml-text — the concatenated text content of the whole subtree (textContent)

column3: the text of a leaf element
text is gathered across nested elements, in document order
an empty element has no text
element-only content yields the empty string

column1: # §3  xml-elem — the element children only (DOM children), dropping text nodes

column3: text nodes are dropped, element children kept in order
an element with no element children yields the empty list
an empty element has no element children

column1: # §4  xml-attr — one attribute value (a String) or None

column3: a present attribute returns its value
a later attribute resolves by name, not position
a missing attribute returns None
an element with no attributes returns None

column1: # §5  deq — structural equality (eq is identity for compounds; deq is the deep one)

column3: two distinct but structurally equal elements are deq
equality recurses through children
different tags are not equal
different attribute values are not equal
a FlexXml and a content-equal immutable element compare equal (flexness is a mode, not identity)

column1: # §6  flex / node — the mutability mode and the freeze back to immutable

column3: flex on a Node/Xml yields a mutable FlexXml
FlexXml conforms to the Xml slot (it IS a Node/Xml)
node freezes a FlexXml back to an immutable Node/Xml
the frozen value is a plain Node/Xml again

column1: # §7  negatives — the accessors require a Node/Xml subject

column3: a Map is not a Node/Xml — xml-text rejects it
a scalar is not a Node/Xml — xml-elem rejects it
a String subject does not match xml-attr's Xml slot
